💡 Key Takeaways
  • Warning: This article contains SPOILERS for Agatha All Along.
  • In a recent development, agatha All Along's central witch coven comprises seven different characters, each with their own specialties, powers, stories, and Marvel connections.
  • Sources indicate that given that WandaVision is one of the better-ranked MCU indicates thus far, Agatha All Along was highly anticipated, especially considering the former show's creator and writer, Jac Schaeffer, possesses the same roles in the latter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning: This article contains SPOILERS for Agatha All Along.

In a recent development, agatha All Along's central witch coven comprises seven different characters, each with their own specialties, powers, stories, and Marvel connections. Agatha All Along's MCU story stems from the climactic ending of WandaVision. The latter show centered on the Scarlet Witch and her inadvertent enslavement of the town of Westview. The villain of the show was Agatha herself, played by Kathryn Hahn once more in Agatha All Along's cast of characters.

Sources indicate that given that WandaVision is one of the better-ranked MCU indicates thus far, Agatha All Along was highly anticipated, especially considering the former show's creator and writer, Jac Schaeffer, possesses the same roles in the latter. What makes Agatha All Along's MCU story even more interesting, however, is the show's fresh batch of characters.

The series is a fun, spooky, Halloween-inspired MCU show centering on witches from across the MCU, meaning each character has their own intriguing stories, power sets, connections to Agatha, and links to Marvel Comics.

Industry observers note that beginning with the titular character, Agatha Harkness is a former witch from Salem, Massachusetts. Agatha belonged to her own coven long ago but was accused of practicing dark magic during the Salem witch trials. After her coven attempted to cast her out, Agatha's dark magic attacked her peers, including her mother, killing them and setting Agatha down a path of villainy and evil. 300 years later, Agatha was drawn to Westview after Wanda Maximoff covered the town in a witch hex, with the former seeking to harness the latter's chaos magic.

It has been revealed that agatha failed to draw Wanda's power from her and had her own drained in the process, leading the latter to enslave the former in Westview seemingly permanently. In Agatha All Along, the titular witch is freed from her prison and embarks on a quest down the Witches Road. At the end of it, Agatha hopes to recover what will make her whole again: her powers.

According to recent reports, in the comics, Agatha's origins are similar to those from WandaVision. Agatha was involved in the Salem Witch Trials in the comics, only with the difference that she orchestrated them to cull the weak from her coven. Over the centuries, Agatha spends a lot of time trying to build her power in multiple covens, training several magic users, and even fighting in wars like the American Revolutionary War and defeating Nazi sorcerers during World War II.

Industry observers note that eventually, Agatha crossed paths with The Fantastic Four when she became the governess of Franklin Richards, often aiding the team and even teaching Franklin to hone his powers. Through The Fantastic Four, she met Wanda Maximoff. Agatha became the mentor to Wanda and other magic owners in the modern Marvel Comics era and has been killed and subsequently resurrected multiple times. In the current continuity, Agatha is alive, though is rarely seen in stories.

Like the other strong sorcerers of the Marvel universe, Agatha's powers are a gateway to almost endless abilities. From energy and elemental manipulation and binding spells to dimensional manipulation, flight, force fields, and illusions, Agatha is one of the most powerful magic people in the Marvel Comics pantheon. This is without mentioning her telepathy, telekinesis, and the tens of other abilities she possesses through her magical training.

According to recent reports, while Agatha's powers are gone in Agatha All Along as a result of Wanda's spell on the witch at the end of WandaVision, it appears Harkness still believes she has the ability to absorb the powers of other magic-people if they direct their abilities at her. However, it's unclear whether this is indeed true, or rather the character's own hopes as she attempts everything to retrieve her former abilities once more.

It has been revealed that one of the other witches who joins Agatha and Teen down the Witches Road is Lilia Calderu, played by Patti LuPone. In the context of Agatha’s coven, Calderu serves as an expert in divination. Divination is the practice of seeking knowledge about the future via supernatural means. In Calderu’s case in Agatha All Along, she suffers from various visions and flashes of foresight, making her seem somewhat more unhinged than the witches around her.

Industry observers note that because of her powers, Lilia is shown to be aware of some of the details of Agatha's past, telling the witch that she knows Agatha has been under the influence of "someone you hurt" and who then took her agency for 3 years. This - combined with Lilia's own experience of witch history, since Agatha suggests she's 450 years old - it's likely Lilia could provide more insight about Agatha's backstory as the show continues, since she's clearly able to access information that the witch may otherwise not be willing to reveal.

According to recent reports, in the comics, Lilia Calderu is the descendant of the first Baron of Mordo. Calderu is part of a coven that is responsible for the protection of the Book of Cagliostro. Interestingly, Lilia is linked to Wanda Maximoff’s origins in Marvel Comics, with her divination powers providing visions that Wanda will become immensely powerful.

Sources indicate that lilia’s story ended with Karl Mordo romancing her to gain her trust. Mordo stole the Book of Cagliostro, breaking Lilia’s heart and leading her down a path of revenge. Despite enlisting the aid of Doctor Strange, Lilia was killed by a Living Gargoyle searching for Mordo.

Industry observers note that agatha All Along will see Alice Wu-Gulliver (Ali Ahn) join the titular character’s coven to journey down the Witches Road. Where Lilia Calderu excels in divination, Alice Wu-Gulliver is described as a protection witch. This means Wu-Gulliver is likely the strongest of the seven regarding shielding spells, and thus will be vital to countering the dangers of the Witches Road.

The character is shown to be using these skills to work in a mall store at the start of Agatha All Along before losing her job, which leads her to decide to join Agatha's coven and travel the Witch's Road, though her past in the armed forces is alluded to as well, suggesting there's much more to be uncovered about Wu-Gulliver. This concept is further hinted at by allusions to Alice Wu-Gulliver's mother, Lorna Wu, who is described as a witch and famous musician, and who appears to have gone mysteriously missing, possibly in the Witch's Road itself.

It has been revealed that ali Ahn described Alice as someone who is looking to access a magical power that has lain dormant for a while. As such, it's possible that her protection abilities will take some time to come to their full extent over the course of the show - which may leave the coven in a precarious position until that time.

Industry observers note that in Marvel Comics, this character is born Alice Gulliver. Alice is the daughter of August Wu, the magical protector of Hong Kong, and the detective Adam Gulliver. Alice desired to become a member of the police force like her father as a teen, around the same time her mother was killed by a demonic figure. After this tragedy, Alice found that her hair had changed color from brown to the red of her mother’s. To compound this sadness, Alice’s father was later killed by one of the Chinese Triads.

In a recent development, eventually, Alice became a police detective like her father, while using the inherited magical powers from her mother to her advantage. Alice started using a shortened version of her mother’s title, “The Wu,” and even teamed up with the Scarlet Witch to defeat the evil wizard Dark Tongji. The title of “The Wu” is being incorporated into Agatha All Along’s version of the character, who is named Alice Wu-Gulliver.

Industry observers note that agatha All Along will include the Marvel Comics character of Jennifer Kale. In Agatha All Along, Jennifer Kale is a potions witch of Agatha's newfound coven, with her skills primarily being found in alchemy and chemistry. Kale is revealed to have had her powers bound, and to be using her knowledge to make a health and beauty business wherein she creates skincare products and probiotic candles, though it's also revealed that she's dealing with an impending legal lawsuit for some of these products, suggesting things aren't going entirely smoothly.

Jennifer has been described by actor Sasheer Zamata as very sarcastic, possessing a love-hate relationship with Agatha herself. Agatha All Along plays on this, implying the pair have a notable history together that is as of yet unexplored.

In Marvel Comics, Jennifer Kale was the daughter of Joshua Kale, leader of the Cult of Zhered-Na. Zhered-Na was a powerful sorceress, with the cult existing in the Florida Everglades where the Nexus of All Realities is housed. Eventually, Jennifer took an interest in witchcraft and began dabbling in magic.

After facing off against demons and having many adventures, resulting in the discovery of a psychic connection with a creature called the Man-Thing, Jennifer became the apprentice of a wizard called Dakimh. Jennifer’s story has led her to become an ally of Ghost Rider, X-Force, and the Midnight Sons.

Recent findings suggest that more so than the previous two witches explored, Jennifer Kale's Marvel Comics powers are more defined. Kale draws magic from three sources: her personal power from training, powers gained by tapping into the magical energy of the Marvel universe, and extra-dimensional powers. These three sources offer Kale a myriad of magic powers, from magic bolts, shields, dimensional portals, and teleportation, to more psychological abilities like affecting memories and charming other people. These powers are very different from Agatha All Along's description of Kale as a witch who specializes in potions.

Recent findings suggest that aubrey Plaza's Rio Vidal is one of Agatha All Along's original characters, though there are rumors she is a gender-swapped version of Marvel Comics' Emerald Warlock. Rio is described as the warrior witch of Agatha's coven, the more badass counterpart to her peers, though it is unclear what her powers are as yet. Speculation that she is Lady Death is also one of the major aspects of her character.

Sources indicate that rio likely has more offensive powers than the shielding, divination, and alchemical powers of her sister witches. Her fight with Agatha early in the show only reveals her fighting powers, but these could possibly have also been enhanced by whatever magic she holds.

The show has subtly suggested Plaza's character is a green witch, since Agatha avoids recruiting an earth witch placed on her list of witches to recruit who is noted to have only a black heart. Instead, Agatha recruits Mrs. Hart - who is very clearly shown to not have powers at this time - and Rio is the only witch who'd seemingly evoke this reaction. When Mrs. Hart dies, the coven summons another green witch, and Rio highlights up.

Recent findings suggest that the final character to make up Agatha's coven in Agatha All Along is, surprisingly, not even a witch as far as the MCU's past stories go: Sharon Davis, a.k.a. Mrs. Hart. Debra Jo Rupp first played this character in WandaVision, with Sharon Davis being a resident of Westview who became "Mrs. Hart" when under the influence of Wanda's hex. WandaVision ended with Sharon being freed from Wanda's control, making her return in Agatha All Along that much more surprising.

In a featurette for Agatha All Along, Sharon is described as the group's green witch, but Sharon was shown as having no distinct powers in WandaVision, and indeed seems to have none in the sequel show, with Agatha tricking her into joining the group. Whether Sharon Davis will become a witch in Agatha All Along remains to be seen, but she at least provides the show with an everyman character, a connection to a past MCU project, and a seventh witch for the coven intent on traveling the Witches Road.

According to recent reports, evanora Harkness was the mother of Agatha Harkness. She first appeared in WandaVision during flashbacks for Agatha, where it was revealed that she was the leader of the Salemites and attempted to murder Agatha during the Salem Witch Trials, accusing Agatha of betraying her coven and practicing the darkest of magic.

She appeared again in episode 5 of Agatha All Along, possessing Agatha during one of the trials. After leaving Agatha's body, Evanora tells the rest of the witches that her "coven risked everything to kill her and you fools have willingly joined her." Evanora reveals that she should have killed Agatha the moment she was born, saying she was "born evil." When Alice casts a spell on Agatha and Evanora, she leaves, keeping what her purpose was to be there a mystery.

Like Agatha and the rest of the coven, Evanora Harkness was proficient in witchcraft, leading her own coven before being killed by Agatha. Through her magic, Evanora was able to manipulate energy to her will. After her death, Evanora Harkness was able to possess Agatha's body during an episode of Agatha All Along, but it is unclear if that is exclusive to her.

In a recent development, the Salem Seven made their MCU debut during the events of Agatha All Along. It is revealed that they are the children of the Salemites, the coven of witches that Agatha murdered during the Salem Witch Trials. They are seen in Agatha All Along attempting to hunt down Agatha and the rest of her coven, gaining access to the Witches' Road to do so.

Agatha spared the children after killing the Salemites, but that led to them growing hateful and resentful, eventually forming a coven to get.

It has been revealed that revenge on Agatha for the murders. With them still pursuing Agatha and her coven, The Salem Seven will presumably be featured in more episodes of Agatha All Along, trying to exact their revenge.

The Salem Seven's comic book origins vary greatly compared to their MCU counterparts. In the comics, they are Nicholas Scratch's children, who is the son of Agatha Harkness. This means that Agatha is their grandmother. This is a massive change from the MCU version being the children of the Salemites, but given that Agatha's son is dead in the universe, it makes sense for them to have a different origin. In the comics, The Salem Seven went after Agatha because Scratch believed Agatha betrayed New Salem by leaving it.

Agatha All Along’s most mysterious character throughout the first five episodes was undoubtedly Joe Locke’s Teen. Eventually, Joe Locke's character was finally confirmed to be Wiccan, after a long period of speculation. It is revealed that it was Wiccan who frees Agatha from Wanda’s Hex and convinces her to take the Witches Road to retrieve her powers.

Whether he has ulterior motives for this remains to be seen, but episode 5 saw him use his powers to overcome the members of the coven, including Agatha, showing there is definitely more to this character than he initially led on.

Wanda lost her children in WandaVision and Doctor Strange 2, meaning Billy’s reincarnation could have taken place. There is still a mystery about just how Billy returned following those projects, but Agatha All Along is primed to reveal even more about his character for the remainder of the series. The two biggest questions revolving around Billy are about who put the spell on him so that no one would hear his name and how he did return.

Given the secrecy surrounding Billy so far, it is difficult to explore his comic book connections. In the comics, Billy was reincarnated from Billy Maximoff, whom the Scarlet Witch created using her reality-altering powers and a lost soul. The devil Mephisto claimed the souls for himself before being destroyed by Wanda’s magic within them. The soul of Billy was then reincarnated into Billy Kaplan, the son of two workers in Newly introduced York City.

According to recent reports, after a difficult early life, Billy found solace in his relationship with Teddy Altman, later revealed to be Hulkling, the son of Captain Marvel. After Billy discovers magical powers, he joins Marvel's Young Avengers with Hulkling, and eventually, they encounter Tommy Shepherd. It is revealed that Billy and Tommy are the reincarnated twins of Wanda and Vision, becoming known by their superhero names, Wiccan and Speed. After this, Billy undergoes several adventures alongside his boyfriend Hulkling, his brother Speed, and his other allies in the Marvel universe.

As the son of Wanda Maximoff, Billy possesses immense magical power. Perhaps his main power is reality manipulation like his mother, with Billy able to use a lot of spells by speaking what he wishes into reality, unlike the more deliberate spells of other wizards and witches. Aside from this, Billy’s other powers include astral projection, magical binding, clairvoyance, concussive blasts, elemental manipulation, flight, healing, and teleportation. Wiccan’s magic is also a gateway to many other abilities, from augmentation and telepathy to telekinesis and transmutation, to name but a few.

Industry observers note that in Agatha All Along, he tells Agatha that he doesn't have any real powers and is looking to traverse the Witch's Road in the hopes of gaining his own. Of course, this was a lie because he uses his powers during the reveal of who he is, and is already quite strong. Why he decided to hide his abilities from Agatha and the rest of the coven is a mystery, and leaves audiences just what his motives are in Agatha All Along.

Agatha Harkness, after the events of "WandaVision," seeks to regain her magical powers. Joining forces with unexpected allies, including the son of an old adversary, she battles upcoming mystical threats while uncovering hidden secrets in the magical realm.

Recent findings suggest that arguably the greatest Christmas franchise of all time is getting its star back. 34 years after 1992's "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York," Macaulay Culkin is set to return as Kevin McCallister in a third movie that will act as a sequel/reboot for the saga.

Recent findings suggest that in July 2026, we got an patch on "Home Alone 3" (as we'll call it until further notice) that suggested Culkin's return was more likely than ever, as the actor reportedly paid a visit to the Disney lot where he met with studio head David Greenbaum. It has been revealed that according to Belloni, the "sequel/reboot" is "officially in development," with longtime writing partners Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg producing under their Point Grey banner. That's good news, as the duo couldn't be better suited to the material. (Disney, of course, has yet to officially confirm any of this.).

In a recent development, ever since "Lost in Latest York," the "Home Alone" franchise has delivered sequel after sequel that didn't need to happen — the most recent being the Mouse House's, to date, one and only attempt, following the Disney/Fox merger, to revitalize the saga with a sixth movie. But "Home Sweet Home Alone" once again failed to bring back Kevin McCallister. Now, however, things look set to change.

In a recent development, in 2025, Macaulay Culkin embarked on a "Nostalgic Night With Macaulay Culkin" tour, during which he spoke about his surprisingly great-sounding idea for a "Home Alone 3" movie. Culkin's film would follow an adult Kevin McCallister who's become too focused on work at the expense of his young son. Kevin would then become locked out of his own house with his son still inside before having to break back in and avoid his son's ingenious traps in what is essentially a metaphor for working his way back into his son's heart. Not bad, right? For now, it remains unclear whether this is, in fact, the pitch Disney has greenlit, but it would make sense.

Recent findings suggest that culkin has seemingly been warming up to the property over the past couple of years. As mentioned, 2025 saw him launch the "Nostalgic Night" tour, during which he chatted positively about his previous two "Home Alone" movies. Then, in 2026, he played a grown-up Kevin in a McDonald's commercial. Now, pending official confirmation from Disney, it seems he'll return to the franchise proper, with Matt Belloni noting how the actor's two young sons likely played into his decision.

Sources indicate that belloni also highlighted the massive popularity of Culkin's first two films, which reliably shoot to the top of the most-watched streaming charts every holiday season. Per FlixPatrol, right on cue, the original "Home Alone" is back in the Disney+ movie charts, jumping from number seven on November 15, 2026, to number two as of the following day, where it sits at the time of writing. The other films in the saga? Nowhere to be seen. Lord knows the "Home Alone" movies need a major revitalization, and you couldn't do better than Culkin's return in that regard.

Is A24 Finally Substantial Enough to Be Considered a Major Studio?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2072 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, earlier this year when IndieWire reported that A24 had settled a dispute with Marcus Theaters over theatrical terms, a back and forth that kept some of A24‘s summer titles like “The Invite,” “Tony,” and “Onslaught” out of the fourth-largest chain in the country, the reason was because of a debate over A24’s size.
  • It has been revealed that this is the question that Hollywood — and even perhaps A24 internally — should start asking: Should A24 now be considered a major studio?
  • In some regards, this is a semantic discussion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, earlier this year when IndieWire reported that A24 had settled a dispute with Marcus Theaters over theatrical terms, a back and forth that kept some of A24‘s summer titles like “The Invite,” “Tony,” and “Onslaught” out of the fourth-largest chain in the country, the reason was because of a debate over A24’s size. When you have blockbusters as big as “Backrooms” and “Marty Supreme,” why would you still want theatrical terms that lump you in with the specialized, little guys?

It has been revealed that this is the question that Hollywood — and even perhaps A24 internally — should start asking: Should A24 now be considered a major studio? Should A24 be in the same conversation as Disney, Universal, Sony, Paramount, Warner Bros., Netflix, Amazon MGM, Apple, and Lionsgate? Related Stories Bill Hader’s Feature Directorial Debut ‘They Know’ Lands at Black Bear Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation.

In some regards, this is a semantic discussion. Whether A24 is in that made-up tier of six to nine corporate conglomerates that the trades call “majors” doesn’t mean a lick to the general public. Audiences know they care about the A24 brand and logo in the same way they pay attention to the brands of Marvel, Pixar, Blumhouse, IMAX, and a select few others making movies today, and the rest is mostly gravy. Postrak found that on average, 70 percent of people who see A24 movies on opening weekend go to theaters more often than others, at least monthly, so the brand has an impact. But whether it has theatrical terms on par with Paramount or with Bleecker Street doesn’t matter in the slightest.

Recent findings suggest that in another sense, whether A24 is a major studio and not some cool upstart indie with a lot of scale matters a whole lot. It matters to investors, it matters to people who care about the A24 brand, it matters to theater owners, and it should matter to A24 itself as it defines what it wants to be moving forward. Netflix wasn’t always considered a major, legacy studio, but their size and success got so undeniable that you had to put them in the same conversation as the other majors who drove trends, who influenced deal making for stars and creators, and who eventually had to reach the same labor terms as everyone else.

A24 might soon be in the same boat, if it isn’t already. Led by the success of “Backrooms,” the company has entered a new echelon in 2026, one that has allowed it to rival studios that were once much larger than A24 in every facet. Now those lines have blurred, A24’s budgets and the grosses those films are able to generate have grown, it’s earning sizable $75 million investments from places like Google and is in the mix to buy properties like Letterboxd, arguably more than others have speculated its time to sell.

Recent findings suggest that answering whether A24 is a “major” isn’t a simple question with one answer. There’s several criteria we could look at to make a case in either direction.

A24 through November 15 in 2026 has earned $526.6 million at the domestic box office, according to data from Rentrak. It was led by “Backrooms,” which made $197 million domestic, but that’s not even half its overall haul. This year, that’s roughly $175 million above the next-highest specialized distributor in Focus Features ($351.8 million), which released the even more successful “Obsession” ($263.4 million) this year, and it’s well above the likes of other indie rivals like Neon, Fathom, GKIDS, Angel Studios, Black Bear, and Searchlight.

It has also more than doubled what it brought in across a full year in 2025, a 124 percent increase so far (it still has its substantial awards play “The Debut” opening in December and “Club Kid” going wider), and it’s nearly four times where it was in 2023 when A24’s total domestic box office was $136.7 million and its biggest release of the year was “Talk to Me,” which made $44.2 million domestic. Four of A24’s movies this year (“Backrooms,” “You Can See Everything,” “The Drama,” and “Primetime”) surpassed that figure.

It’s safe to say it puts A24 in a tier of its own above the other indies. But does it rise to the level of a major? As recently as last year, the answer was squarely no. But A24 in 2026, per Rentrak, commands a 6.0 percent market share on the year so far. That puts it fifth on the year so far, ahead of Warner Bros., Paramount, and Lionsgate (those numbers will change as some other tentpoles emerge). It would not have even cracked the top 10 last year when its market share was just 2.7 percent and was largely driven by the late-year success of “Marty Supreme.”.

Sources indicate that A24 doesn’t have and probably won’t for some time field a movie that can realistically sniff $1 billion worldwide the way many major studios manage to pump out each and every year. But receipts don’t lie, and what makes this realistically sustainable for A24 to repeat year after year is how much it has grown.

A24 is releasing in the vicinity of 16 to 18 movies annually, and that puts it easily on par with legacy studios like Disney, Sony, Warner Bros., and Paramount. Skydance, which now owns Paramount and WB, will release 30+ movies a year, but between the two studios. Universal tends to get into the 20s, but only when you combine its output with that of Focus. Netflix puts out way, way more than the whole bunch, but they’re naturally streaming movies that include low-budget genre movies and documentaries.

In a recent development, some of A24’s films each year are still acquisitions out of festivals, which was the case this year with both “The Invite” (Sundance) and “Club Kid” (Cannes). But like the other majors, A24 produces and finances a large majority of its movies independently, with a handful of co-productions. Importantly, it works with newly introduced filmmakers and forges relationships so that they stay in their pipeline, whether they’re newcomers like Lance Oppenheim and Kane Parsons or veterans like Celine Song, Alex Garland, and Ari Aster who have returned to A24 time and again.

Industry observers note that A24’s international distribution has it partnering with other overseas distributors, which is structurally different from major studios that have robust international distribution arms, but it has still released some of its movies in English-language territories like the UK. You can imagine that as A24 continues to grow, that could be one area of natural expansion.

Where A24 still lags significantly behind other majors though is in its overall content spend, a number that A24 doesn’t publicly disclose. Netflix had a content spend this year of about $20 billion. Disney was around $24 billion and recently projected to increase to $26 billion in its next fiscal year. Maybe if A24 starts picking up sports rights to the NBA it can start getting into that ballpark.

According to recent reports, but even when focusing just on film, something like “Backrooms” was still produced for a modest $10 million, whereas other studios have multiple titles that well exceed $100 million in production budget alone. We do know though that its budgets have increased dramatically as A24 pursues more tentpole properties. “Marty Supreme” was previously its most expensive title, but its adaptation of the video game “Elden Ring” will blow that out of the water, with a budget in the vicinity of $170 million or above. That kind of investment carries risks. There are Marvel movies that don’t cost that much.

A24 hasn’t yet put its stamp on a four-quadrant, animated Dr. Seuss movie or something similar that would easily make you think it has ambitions of becoming a major studio, but the types of movies it has released has grown more varied over the years. It has horror movies, adult comedies, biopics, thrillers, and even, of course, documentaries like “You Can See Everything,” an area that it looked like A24 was scaling back on not too long ago. When “Elden Ring” opens it will squarely be an action fantasy, and the studio has other genre films, comedies, thrillers, and more in the works for next year.

Sources indicate that you can also see A24’s diversity in how it’s approaching awards plays versus commercial titles or specialized fare. Something like “The Drama” this year opened wide right out of the gate given its star power, whereas others like “The Invite” and “Tony” have stuck to platform releases before going wider. And those smaller, art house titles alongside its genre movies and its tentpoles are still a key part of its business model and identity. Movies like “Pillion,” “Mother Mary,” and “The Moment” have done business on a much smaller scale, but are still key in helping the tech giant get to that 6 percent share (they lost money on some, though).

Sources indicate that the definition of major studio today has evolved to the point that the movie division is just a component of a massive media conglomerate, one that also includes television, streaming, gaming, sports, news, theme parks, and other ancillary businesses. If you’re Apple or Amazon, your movie studio is a small cog, practically a loss leader, in the larger tech empire. It gives these companies valuations of tens of billions of dollars, and it’s why A24 could still be a target for M&A if it chooses to sell.

According to recent reports, A24 does have its own record label for music and original movie score releases and vinyl pressing, it has been producing a podcast since 2018, it owns the Cherry Lane Theater in Latest York for stage productions and concerts, it sells plenty of kooky merchandise, and it even has a membership program and campus ambassador program that have seen growth in recent years. They’re all things that suggest the company has more on its mind than movies.

Recent findings suggest that and as we wrote earlier this week, its TV unit has quietly had as strong a year as its film team. A24 has spread series across virtually every major streaming service, all of them again varying in genre, pedigree, and budget. It’s not just the number of reveals that has expanded but the executive team to support them.

It may be a strength that A24 doesn’t have its own SVOD service to support all these shows and movies, or a broadcast network or cable channel that could further complicate things. Those businesses are very costly to operate and some are in the decline phase of their trajectories. Yet, it inherently keeps A24 in a lower tier compared to other major studios that do have their own distribution apparatus for television and can license content from other studios like A24. While Gen Z might get excited about the idea of an A24 streaming service, that’s an area of growth that’s less likely to occur in the short term. Well, unless A24 wants to raise a lot more capital.

In a recent development, this is the qualitative assessment of whether A24 should be considered a “major” studio, the one that doesn’t lean on numbers and instead just goes on feel. A24 might argue that it is one of one, that it doesn’t belong to the world of major studios, and that the baggage that comes with that status isn’t worth it. But its leaders probably believe A24 is a step above the other indies that are almost solely distributors. Do we really think the same company that is taking a chance on movies as weird as “You Can See Everything” or “Primetime” is equivalent to a studio that might make the odd “Digger,” but is mostly interested in producing “A Minecraft Movie” and “Superman?” Is it fair to lump in A24 with Focus, Searchlight, and Sony Pictures Classics, which are quite literally just specialized labels within larger studios?

All that could be true, but it doesn’t mean we shouldn’t reassess how we view A24 as a company or how we handicap its hits and misses in the same way we would with Disney or Netflix. Even if we’re not ready to call A24 a “major,” there’s certainly a major shift in where A24 sits in this industry. With great success comes an even greater spotlight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 players weren't kidding about wanting to spend the game's entire launch day in Leonida. Much hullabaloo was made about people requesting time off from work or faking sick to spend the entire day playing GTA 6, and plenty of companies tried to capitalize on that conversation with marketing stunts.

Mat Piscatella, senior director at market research firm Circana, shared data on Friday about just how much time players spent with GTA 6 on its launch day, Thursday, Nov. 19. "PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494," he stated in a post on Bluesky. That's an average of 8.55 and 8.23 hours for PS5 and Xbox players, respectively. That means GTA 6 players effectively spent the length of a workday stealing drugs, beating up rednecks, driving around Fake Florida, kicking bodega cats, and playing GTA 6's in-game video games.

Recent findings suggest that you could fly from Fresh York City to Seattle in under 8.55 hours. You could watch the entirety of the original Star Wars trilogy in under 8.55 hours. You could binge The Office season 4 in under 8.55 hours. You could finish Resident Evil 2 in under 8.55 hours, and probably still have enough time to finish it again. You could get an honest-to-god good night's sleep for under 8.55 hours, on average. All I'm saying is, 8.55 hours is a long time, especially for an average.

Recent findings suggest that the average playtime stat is certainly eye-catching, but other numbers Piscatella shared are perhaps even more staggering. 61% of US-based PlayStation 5 players and 56% of global Xbox Series X players "engaged" with GTA 6 on its launch day, figures Piscatella called "absolutely bonkers." He used Fortnite to put that in perspective: Epic Games' battle royale was the second-most played game on Nov. 19 with 10% of PlayStation and Xbox players engaging with it.

Those numbers are as unbelievable as GTA 6's sales figures. According to Take-Two Interactive, GTA 6's launch is now the biggest entertainment launch in history with $3.79 billion generated in revenue.

Tech Report: 9 Video Game Sequels Better Than the Original

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in theory, sequels should always be better than the original since it is easier to see the flaws of the first and correct them.
  • In a recent development, that is why this list will feature eight video game sequels that are better than the original based on aspects such as improvements, design, gameplay, narrative, originality, fan opinion, critical acclaim, and overall quality.
  • Recent findings suggest that games on this list don’t specifically need to be the second game in a franchise, as long as they are a sequel, which opens the door for Baldur’s Gate 3.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in theory, sequels should always be better than the original since it is easier to see the flaws of the first and correct them. However, sometimes it’s too difficult to capture the certain magic that the first title had, and this is especially true for video games like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. However, that isn’t always true, with some sequels not only living up to the hype, but also becoming better video games.

In a recent development, that is why this list will feature eight video game sequels that are better than the original based on aspects such as improvements, design, gameplay, narrative, originality, fan opinion, critical acclaim, and overall quality. These games took the base of something great and made it even better, becoming the definitive version and a sequel that improved on almost everything. Please note that Red Dead Redemption 2 will not be on this list because it is a prequel, not a sequel.

Recent findings suggest that games on this list don’t specifically need to be the second game in a franchise, as long as they are a sequel, which opens the door for Baldur’s Gate 3. When the player is infected by a Mind Flayer parasite, they will turn into one if they don’t find a cure for themselves. Teaming up with others in their position, gamers travel across the country in search of this concoction, but the brewing war between gods and mortals makes this much more complicated.

Baldur’s Gate 3 is the most recent game on this list, but it didn’t take long to become one of the most influential titles of all time. This is the ultimate role-playing experience, improving on the narrative, scale, gameplay, graphics, and options. Baldur’s Gate 3 is as good a sequel as it can get, even if this entire franchise is home to masterpieces. There is so much love and passion put into this game, and fans can feel it in every ounce of the design, which is exactly what every sequel should have.

Recent findings suggest that batman is one of the biggest superheroes of all time, with his presence extending from comics to movies and even video games. Batman: Arkham City puts Bruce Wayne into the titular prison, which is a walled-off section of Gotham City. Donning the cap and cowl, players must learn of Protocol 10, the mysterious plan Hugo Strange has set, but first, Batman needs to take care of the many villains trying to kill him.

Batman: Arkham Asylum is a fantastic game, but most fans will agree the sequel is much better. The open-world allowed for more engaging traversal, the narrative was tenser and had fewer errors, and the gameplay was extended with more combos, making it one of the best martial arts video games. It is the perfect follow-up to an already incredible video game, arguably establishing itself as the definitive Batman experience not just in video games, but overall.

Resident Evil is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026, with massive projects such as Resident Evil Requiem and the film directed by Zach Cregger. However, nothing can compare to Resident Evil 4, the best sequel in the franchise. When the daughter of the president is kidnapped by a cult in Spain, Leon S. Kennedy goes to save her. But when he learns the cult has been infected by a parasite, survival and escape become even more difficult.

The first Resident Evil is great, but most of the sequels are better than it, especially Resident Evil 4. While polarizing to some, the changes made in Resident Evil 4 revitalized the franchise, adding stylish action mechanics and an over-the-shoulder camera view. It was simple, but very effective, making this game way easier to play than other titles while maintaining the core difficulty and fun. Resident Evil 4 is a horror masterpiece and a sequel that is one of the best games ever.

According to recent reports, it was recently declared that EA shut down BioWare, the game studio that brought fans so many classics, including the Mass Effect franchise. Each game is nearly perfect, but Mass Effect 2 in particular stands out as one of the best. Years after the first game, Commander Shepard is killed in the line of duty, only to be revived shortly after. Those who brought him back to life task him with investigating a mysterious alien race that has abducted entire human colonies, harvesting people to build a upcoming threat to the entire galaxy.

It has been revealed that the first Mass Effect was a terrific video game that established the beloved formula, and this sequel took what was great in that and expanded on it. The first bright spot is the fact that progress from the first game is saved in the sequel, creating an interconnected feel that makes decisions long-term. Mass Effect 2 strips away the original inventory management, repetitive exploration, and stiff shooting, replacing them with improved mechanics and design for a much better experience. With the gameplay greatly improved, it could then focus on what the franchise is best known for: the worldbuilding, which is what makes Mass Effect 2 one of the best sci-fi video games for beginners.

Assassin’s Creed is one of the best historical video game franchises of all time, and while it has changed its formula to be more mythological and open-world RPG, the roots of historical stealth are unmatched, and that is highlighted by Assassin’s Creed II. Set in Renaissance Italy during the late 15th century, the story follows Ezio, a young Florentine nobleman whose father and brothers are framed for treason and publicly executed. He dons his father’s assassin robes and embarks on a quest for vengeance against those who wronged him, including the Templar Order.

When it comes to superior sequels, Assassin’s Creed II is a textbook example, transforming the foundation into a player-driven experience. Adding mission variety, this mix of tasks built a much better experience in terms of gameplay, and set in the gorgeous Renaissance cities, it was a true joy to explore. Ezio is also regarded as the best protagonist in the franchise, and it isn’t hard to see why, providing a decades-spanning character arc that shows his entire evolution. Assassin’s Creed II is a complete overhaul that creates the quintessential game in the franchise.

Sources indicate that the Witcher franchise is at an all-time high, with a TV show adaptation, newly introduced DLC, and a sequel, which all started because of the popularity of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Geralt of Rivia is a Witcher, but he must put aside his usual monster-hunting gig in order to save Ciri, his adoptive daughter, from the titular spectral group that wants to use her powers for evil.

This article contains spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.".

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" adapts the story that fans have been waiting for since 2008, revealing how Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), future mentor of Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence), became the victor of the 50th Hunger Games. Haymitch's games were even more brutal than usual: as a special "quarter quell" game, each of the twelve districts had to offer up four children, not two. (Haymitch ends up in the games after one of the two District 12 boys originally chosen tries to flee and then is shot.).

One of the District 12 kids "reaped" alongside Haymitch is Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), the daughter of a candy shop owning family. A jewelry collector, Maysilee is the original owner of the Mockingjay pin that Katniss eventually comes to wear during the "Hunger Games" trilogy.

Now, this being a prequel where Haymitch's victory (as pyrrhic as it is) is assured, you should go into "Sunrise on the Reaping" knowing Maysilee doesn't walk out of that arena. Grace actually plays two roles in the film, the other being Maysilee's twin sister, Merrilee. Once Haymitch returns, during Maysilee's funeral, he has to see the very same face of the girl he failed.

According to recent reports, viewers, too, might recognize Maysilee and Merrilee's shared face. Mckenna Grace is a prolific young actress with many film and TV (including voiceover) roles to her name. In just the past few years, she appeared in "Five Nights at Freddy's 2" as paranormal activity hunter Lisa, Clara in the Colleen Hoover adaptation "Regretting You," and Hannah Thurman in "Scream 7." Those recent roles only scratch the surface of her acting resume.

In a recent development, born in 2006, Mckenna Grace is a recently graduated child actress; her first acting role was on the 2012 Disney XD series "Crash and Bernstein." Soon after she had a part on soap opera "The Young and the Restless" from 2013 to 2015 as Faith Newman. Her breakout film role was in 2017 Chris Evans vehicle "Gifted," where she played young math prodigy Mary Adler.

In the late 2010s, Grace found a niche playing child versions of main characters. She played young Tonya Harding in "I, Tonya," young Carol Danvers in "Captain Marvel," a young Sabrina Spellman in one episode of "The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina," and starred in Mike Flanagan's miniseries "The Haunting of Hill House" as a young version of Kate Siegel's character Theo Crain. This means she's played young versions of Margot Robbie, Brie Larson, and Kiernan Shipka. (Grace, who played Paige Swanson on sitcom "Young Sheldon," has stated she envisions Reese Witherspoon as the adult version of that character.).

It has been revealed that from 2021 to 2022, during Seasons 4 and 5 of "The Handmaid's Tale," Grace played Esther Keyes, the abused teenage wife of a much older man. This role earned her an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actress in a Drama Series. 2021 was also the year that Grace starred in "Ghostbusters: Afterlife" as Phoebe Spangler, later reprising the role in 2024's "Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire.".

One of Grace's voiceover roles was playing a young version of Daphne Blake in the 2020 animated "Scooby Doo!" film "Scoob!" Fresh off of "Sunrise on the Reaping," she's going to play Daphne again, this time in live-action, in the upcoming TV series "Scooby Doo: Origins" due out in 2027.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is playing in theaters.

Industry observers note that when you first get started in Grand Theft Auto 6, Jason isn't exactly the most fiscally responsible person, and one of the first things you learn is that he's been keeping his money underneath the floorboards in his bedroom. Throughout the first chapter, you can actually deposit money into the floorboard stash anytime, and up until you open up your BuckMe account, this is really the only means of storing your money. However, players who are putting away a ton of cash in Jason's house are in for a rude awakening.

!!! WARNING: THIS GUIDE CONTAINS SPOILERS FOR CHAPTER 2 OF GRAND THEFT AUTO 6 !!!

Without giving too many story details away, players will essentially start Chapter 2 with almost no money due to the climactic ending of Chapter 1. If you're wondering where all the money went that you'd been storing in Jason's floorboards, I've got bad news for you: it's all gone.

Industry observers note that you can return to Jason's house at the start of Chapter 2, but any money you deposited in the floorboard safe will no longer be there. It's a major blow that players likely won't be expecting, and if you've been planning on spending that money later down the road, the story is designed in a way that you really won't be able to recover those funds.

Instead of depositing money into the floorboards at Jason's house, my advice is to invest as much money as you can during Chapter 1 into upgrades, gear, etc., and max out your BuckMe family savings account. Any money you don't spend will essentially be lost when you start Chapter 2, and the story is largely rooted in Lucia and Jason starting from scratch and climbing their way back from the bottom by doing odd jobs across Leonida.

That mentioned, starting in Chapter 2, you will finally be able to claim the "Rainy Day Funds" envelope that's under the floorboards at Jason's house. This is, of course, a separate stash of money than the cash you earned and deposited there during Chapter 1, and was unaffected by the events of Chapter 2's conclusion despite the cash sitting right next to it being lost.

The "Rainy Day Fund" envelope contains $5000 and will come in very useful at the start of Chapter 2, but getting to Jason's house from the motel in Chapter 2 is quite a trek. Additionally, you'll be able to collect the family photos of Lucia and Jason that were in the box, and if you were worried about Lucia and Jason's pet snake Delores, she's safe and sound under the stairs and is sitting on a little surprise as well.

According to recent reports, further, if you're planning to return to Jason's house early in Grand Theft Auto 6 Chapter 2, note that it's heavily guarded by police and you'll need to use stealth in order to claim the "Rainy Day Fund" envelope. If you're being chased or alert the police, they'll shoot on site and you will not be able to grab the money or pictures.

A smoke break at the Signature Theatre ultimately resulted in one of Lois Smith‘s most fascinating performances. The Tony Award winner met Zane Pais while they were both grabbing a quick cigarette while rehearsing plays. Pais had been an admirer of Smith’s work in stage productions like “The Inheritance” and films such as “Marjorie Prime” and “Five Easy Pieces,” and longed to collaborate.

In a recent development, “She has the most amazing delivery of lines; she’s always able to do something so unexpected with the language,” Pais noted during a recent Zoom interview with Smith. “I’ve seen Lois my whole life in so many amazing highlights, just be so unbelievably present on stage and be such a generous actor, and just give these heartfelt and unexpected performances. I’m a major fucking fan.” Related Stories Is A24 Finally Big Enough to Be Considered a Major Studio? Bill Hader’s Feature Directorial Debut ‘They Know’ Lands at Black Bear.

So Pais wrote a short film, “Lightning Bug,” with Smith in mind. In it, she plays Lydia, a fiercely independent nonagenarian who is being pressured into selling the family home by her son and granddaughter. But things take an unexpected turn when a strange young man crashes their dinner, giving Lydia a chance to demonstrate she hasn’t missed a step despite her advanced age.

It has been revealed that “It was all there in the script,” Smith, who recently turned 96, noted. “It wasn’t complex for me to pull it off even though the script is complex.”.

The role did require Smith to perform some fight choreography, but she seemed more nervous about singing a song on screen.

“I really worried: Am I going to be able to do this?” Smith mentioned. “They made me a tape, and I listened to it and listened to it and practiced. I was nervous, but it went all right.”.

“Lightning Bug” filmed over a weekend in the upstate New York home of one of Pais’s relatives. It was true no-frills, all-hands effort. The cast and crew bunked in an Airbnb, and a friend of Pais’s cooked meals for everyone.

Industry observers note that “It felt like we were part of a theater troupe,” Pais said. “We’d work hard. Then in the evenings, we would have red wine and smoke cigarettes.”.

According to recent reports, “I seldom smoke,” Smith interjected. “Occasionally, I’ll smoke other people’s cigarettes.”.

It has been revealed that “Lightning Bug” has won awards on the festival circuit and is Academy Awards eligible this season. The film also stars Bubba Weiler, Josh Hamilton, and Anna Baryshnikov. Here’s the full short:.

This article contains spoilers for "MobLand" Season 2, Episode 10, "The Queen is Dead.".

In a recent development, just when you think the Harrigans might catch a break, things blow up in their face. This time, a car literally blew up in the face of Tom Hardy's Harry Da Souza and his daughter, Gina Da Souza (Teddie Allen), during a frenetic "MobLand" Season 2 finale which almost ended without anyone kicking the bucket. In the episode's final moments, however, we witness what is surely the most shocking death in the entire series, when Joanne Froggatt's Jan Da Souza gets blown sky high thanks to Anson Boon's Eddie Harrigan.

Industry observers note that "Mobland" started life as a "Ray Donovan" spin-off, with Hardy set to play the English equivalent of Liev Schreiber's fixer — which he still sort of does. But his Harry is much darker, colder, and quietly ruthless. Alan Ritchson once compared playing Jack Reacher to playing an alligator waiting to strike. If that's true, then Hardy's Da Souza is a human nuclear warhead, sitting at the head of a ballistic missile and waiting to reduce the world to ashes. Thus far, despite the many challenges endured by the Harrigans in "MobLand" Season 2, he's managed to maintain his icy exterior. Now that his wife has gone up in flames, however, I get the feeling that reservoir of repressed rage is going to come flooding out in Season 3.

In a recent development, season 2, Episode 10 has a deceptive title. When I first saw "The Queen is Dead" on the Paramount+ interface, I thought Maeve Harrigan's (Helen Mirren) days were numbered. But it turns out Jan was the one to pay the piper, and if anyone was going to go down in the season finale, she was surely the least deserving.

Industry observers note that early on, "Mobland" Season 2 proved that it hadn't lost a step in comparison to the first run of episodes. It might even have outdone Season 1, thanks in large part to Johnny Flynn as villain Frankie Cooper, who has been a non-stop delight to watch as the flamboyant, psychopathic London gangster. But the show's been firing on all cylinders from the very first episode of Season 2, in which Pierce Brosnan's Conrad Harrigan dual-wielded his way through an entire gang at a race track.

In a recent development, since then, we've seen the Harrigan crime family come close to collapse. A campaign of violence waged by Frankie at the behest of corrupt U.S. Ambassador Katherine "Kat" McAllister (Janet McTeer) almost wiped out the Harrigans for good. In the season finale, however, Harry Da Souza pulls off an impossibly brilliant plan to finally oust Kat and capture Frankie, all while restoring his criminal employers to their former glory. Jan Da Souza's only real crime (apart from shooting Alex Fine's Donnie) has been sticking around while Harry Da Souza and his criminal cohorts engage in ever more dangerous conduct. Otherwise, she's about as innocent as a "MobLand" character can be.

Recent findings suggest that now, with "MobLand" Season 3 already in production, the question becomes, what sort of fallout will we see from this shocking turn of events? 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 1972, Walter Hill was a young screenwriter with just one produced movie (“Hickey & Boggs”) behind him when he scored an enviable gig: adapting Jim Thompson’s tough-as-nails crime novel “The Getaway” for actor/producer Steve McQueen (then one of the biggest movie stars in the world) and director Sam Peckinpah (then, as now, one of the greatest directors who ever lived).
  • According to recent reports, “The Getaway” screened as part of the museum’s “Branch Selects” series, in which the Academy’s various branches program films they feel exemplify their crafts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 1972, Walter Hill was a young screenwriter with just one produced movie (“Hickey & Boggs”) behind him when he scored an enviable gig: adapting Jim Thompson’s tough-as-nails crime novel “The Getaway” for actor/producer Steve McQueen (then one of the biggest movie stars in the world) and director Sam Peckinpah (then, as now, one of the greatest directors who ever lived). On Wednesday night, Hill spoke before a packed screening at the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures and looked back on the movie that jump-started not only his screenwriting endeavors, but a directing career that would ultimately include classics like “The Warriors,” “48hrs.,” and “Streets of Fire.” Related Stories Short Film ‘Lightning Bug’ Gives Stage and Screen Legend Lois Smith One of Her Greatest Roles — Watch It Here Is A24 Finally Major Enough to Be Considered a Major Studio?

According to recent reports, “The Getaway” screened as part of the museum’s “Branch Selects” series, in which the Academy’s various branches program films they feel exemplify their crafts. “The Getaway” was, appropriately enough, selected by the writers branch, and screenwriter and Academy Governor Larry Karaszewski was on hand to introduce the movie and moderate the pre-screening discussion with Hill. Karaszewski, a longtime “Getaway” enthusiast who carried newspaper ads from the movie around in his wallet when he was 10 years old, pointed out that Hill changed the entire architecture of screenwriting when he burst onto the scene in the early 1970s.

“ Walter, right off the bat, changed the art of screenwriting,” Karaszewski said. “We have an award show here at the Oscars called the Sci-Tech Awards, where they give awards to things that silently change the industry and advance them into the future. I really feel that Walter Hill did that in screenwriting, but it wasn’t a technical advancement. It was a literary advancement. He changed what a page should look like as a screenplay and what it could feel like to read it.” Karaszewski went on to illustrate his point by projecting pages from Robert Bolt’s “Doctor Zhivago” screenplay and Walter Hill’s “Hard Times” side by side on the screen.

Recent findings suggest that “You don’t even have to read [Bolt’s script], just look at it,” Karaszewski noted, pointing out the dense blocks of words compared to Hill’s lean, spare page. “You’re looking at monoliths. It’s dense, and there are camera moves and references to things you would never see on screen. Walter Hill taught screenwriters that you can strip all that away. You can still direct on the page, but not by calling for specific camera movements — just by saying what you’re seeing. Walter’s scripts are made out of short sentences and white space. He looked at the placement of each line as part of the storytelling. He turned the carriage return into an art form.”.

It has been revealed that as Karaszewski welcomed Hill to the stage, he pointed out that “The Getaway” — a smart, terse tale of a couple (Steve McQueen and Ali MacGraw) on the run after their involvement in a botched bank robbery — represented the emergence of Hill’s developing voice. “You’ll already see the beginnings of that remarkable style, the economy, the precision, the sense that every line is pushing you toward the next image.” Yet, as Hill revealed in his lively conversation with Karaszewski, the ruthless efficiency of the pacing and the concentrated emotional impact of “The Getaway” were not easily arrived at.

“I think it’s much harder to adapt than it is to write an original, which is the reverse of the normal theory,” Hill said. “With an original, it’s just you at your desk with the typewriter or pen. When you’re adapting, that almost always means that somebody else owns it, so you’re not simply writing based on your own opinions about what should be in and what should be out, but there’s the producer’s opinion, and the studio’s, and the actor’s. There were all these political currents that one had to navigate.”.

According to recent reports, one such political current came from megastar McQueen, who didn’t interfere much with Hill’s writing but did have one caveat that amused the screenwriter. “He wanted to play a reasonably sympathetic outlaw,” Hill said. “That was not in the Thompson sensibility. So we already had a disparity, but the producer wanted to keep Steve happy.”.

“The Getaway” began as an assignment not for Peckinpah, but for Peter Bogdanovich, who was white-hot coming off of successes like “The Last Picture Show” and “What’s Up, Doc?” Bogdanovich didn’t last long, however, given his clashes with McQueen and McQueen’s power as the film‘s star. “I couldn’t imagine two more diverse sensibilities than Steve and Peter,” Hill said, noting that he had his own disagreements with Bogdanovich over the movie’s tone but wasn’t in a position to argue. “You’ve got to remember, I was nobody. I had one screen credit. And these were significant players.”.

The massive players included not only Bogdanovich and McQueen, but MacGraw, hot off of the smash hit “Love Story.” MacGraw was pushed into the movie by her husband, Paramount studio chief Robert Evans, which Hill found amusing given the way everything played out. “I’m going to tread lightly here,” Hill said of the behind-the-scenes melodrama involving MacGraw leaving Evans when she fell in love with McQueen. “When the material was optioned and I was hired, Bob saw the movie as a fabulous idea for Steve and Ali. It didn’t work out so well for him.”.

After Bogdanovich and McQueen butted heads, Bogdanovich was let go and Peckinpah, who McQueen had enjoyed working with on “Junior Bonner,” came in to take his place. “We were very lucky to get such a talented guy, obviously,” Hill mentioned. “I thought of him then and I think of him now as one of the great directors with a very unique sensibility. I was very privileged to work with him — which doesn’t mean he and I agreed about everything.”.

Hill’s biggest disagreement with Peckinpah had to do with a scene in which MacGraw’s character considered killing McQueen before turning the gun on his nemesis — and the man with whom MacGraw had gone to bed to secure McQueen’s early release from prison. This was a scene carried over from the book, which was darker and more paranoid than what made it to the screen given McQueen’s mandate that he be sympathetic. Hill felt that the moment no longer worked now that the relationship between McQueen and MacGraw was softer and more relatable in the novel.

It has been revealed that “I thought that for the movie we were trying to make, you might forgive your wife for sleeping with a bad man to do a very good thing for you,” Hill noted. “That seemed to be to be conceivable. But if your wife fell into cahoots with the bad guy and actually was thinking about killing you and actually turned the gun on you before she decided to shoot the other guy…this did not track for me. But this is the screenwriter’s dilemma: you either talk the director into your point of view, or you make the change that he wants — or somebody else will. Those are your choices.”.

Sources indicate that hill lost the argument but liked the movie Peckinpah made in the end. “He staged it beautifully,” Hill said. “He shot it beautifully. It’s got one of Steve’s best performances. And the movie turned out to be his greatest hit. He used to call me every once in a while after I became a director and say, ‘Write me another one.'” Ironically, it was the success of “The Getaway” that put Hill in a position where didn’t have to write for other directors anymore.

Industry observers note that “Larry Gordon had a producing deal to make low-budget movies at Columbia,” Hill stated. “He would give young writers a chance to direct, because he said, ‘Even if they’re no good as directors, at least we’ll get a good script. Most of the directors I’m working with aren’t any good anyway.'” Gordon gave Hill the opportunity to direct “Hard Times,” and the rest was history. Aside from kicking off Hill’s directing career, the collaboration became the first of many between the two men. “He’s a wonderful guy and a wonderful producer.”.

Recent findings suggest that now in his 80s, Hill continues to write and direct (his last film was the exquisite character-driven Western “Dead for a Dollar“), plying his trade in the world of graphic novels in between film projects. “I’ve had four of them published in France,” Hill remarked, joking that the only one published in America was “the least good of them,” but promising another one on the way. “You’ve got to keep your hand in somehow.”.

Breaking: Why The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Is The Darkest Movie In The Series

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It's rare for a franchise to get better after 4 or 5 movies, especially when they are prequels that explore questions no one needed answered.
  • And yet, when it comes to "Hunger Games," not only has the franchise improved with time, but the two spin-off prequels are arguably better than even the original series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The following post contains spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.".

It's rare for a franchise to get better after 4 or 5 movies, especially when they are prequels that explore questions no one needed answered. It didn't work for "Star Wars," it didn't work for "Harry Potter," and it shouldn't work for "Hunger Games." At best, these prequels just introduced characters that don't matter in the large scheme of things because everything they do or accomplish gets erased in the original story, at worst they try so hard to answer questions no one cares about that it ends up tarnishing the original work.

And yet, when it comes to "Hunger Games," not only has the franchise improved with time, but the two spin-off prequels are arguably better than even the original series. The latest film, "Sunrise on the Reaping" deepens what came before, while introducing upcoming characters that are as engaging as those we know and add to the larger worldbuilding of Panem. Or, as /Film's review puts it, "Beyond the shock value, this story remains human, emotional, and gripping from beginning to end.".

Sources indicate that even if this movie doesn't have the compelling romance that was central to "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," it delivers a harrowing tale of rebellion. What's more, this is somehow the darkest movie in the "Hunger Games" series, and it's not even close. Not just in terms of deaths — though there are some truly brutal deaths in the movie (which are somehow tamer than the book!) — but also in the overall tone the movie explores. This is the "Hunger Games" equivalent of "Andor" or "Rogue One," a bleak tragedy about one man who dared stand up against a tyrannical government and paid for it with everything he had.

Sources indicate that the "Hunger Games" movies are full of death and suffering; it's part of the game. But "Sunrise on the Reaping" takes it to another level. Though it takes a long while before the nearly 3-hour runtime gets to the actual games, there's a feeling of hopelessness from the first moment. Early on, a kid gets shot for trying to escape the Reaping. Later, on the day of the opening ceremony, the youngest tribute from District 12, Loella, gets brutally killed in a chariot accident.

In a recent development, but it's not just the fact that there are plenty of deaths, or that they're horrible to watch. Sure, seeing poor Ampert get completely mauled by a swarm of cute forest animals and Maysilee Donner getting gored to death by birds is harrowing. The Capitol doesn't just kill children; it tortures them and pulls them apart and makes their parents watch.

According to recent reports, indeed, more than the deaths themselves, it's the meanness around them that makes this movie stand out. When Loella dies, it isn't a murder done by another tribute trying to get an advantage. Instead, it's an accident caused by Capitol audiences throwing flares at the parade circuit knowing full well it will cause the chariot horses to go berserk, because they want to see the tributes suffer. Compared to every other "Hunger Games" movie, the tributes are not only livestock sent to slaughter, or pawns in a political game. Here, they are subjects of absolute torture, playthings to be slowly toyed with and brutalized before getting discarded for the pleasure of others.

We especially see this in the presence of Ampert, whom we learn is only in the games as a punishment for his father Beetee's rebellious activities. Beetee is forced to mentor his own son and then watch him die.

According to recent reports, throughout "Sunrise on the Reaping," there is a sense of hopelessness and inevitability. We know that, eventually, the Hunger Games end and the Capitol falls — but the characters in the movie don't know that. At every turn, Haymitch and his allies see their every effort get squashed and mocked. Their attempts at leveling the playfield just a little bit are met with overwhelming force. Even before the games begin, Haymitch knows he'll never get to go back home because President Snow has personally seen to it that Haymitch dies for his insubordination during the opening ceremony.

According to recent reports, then we get to the third act, where the movie just becomes a cruel feel-bad experience, as Plutarch Heavensbee convinces Snow to let Haymitch survive to prolong his suffering. Haymitch is forced to watch Maysilee die brutally at the hands of waterbird mutts while he is virtually unscathed. Then, even after he wins the games, Haymitch discovers that the televised games were heavily edited to make him look selfish and cowardly, a traitor to every one of his allies, who won only because he was lucky. As if that wasn't enough, Haymitch has to see his family and his girlfriend die horrible deaths after he goes back home from the death games, in what's without a doubt the most nihilistic ending in the franchise.

Industry observers note that it makes sense, however. "Sunrise on the Reaping" takes place at a pivotal moment in the "Hunger Games" timeline, at the height of President Snow's power. We are far removed from the games being almost canceled due to lack of interest like in the previous movie, but also far removed from the simmering rebellion of the original movies. Here, Snow gets away with everything, and he relishes in the cruelty of his games.

If you’re looking for horror or drama with a healthy dose of disturbing material, Netflix has two options: Insidious: Out of the Further follows a mom plagued by awful nightmares that might be missives from a parallel dimension; Gentle Monster follows a pianist and a mother who moves to the country with her family looking for a break from city life. Then her husband is accused by the police of serious crimes.

According to recent reports, other horror movies are available on VOD. There’s The Ice Cream Man, following an ice cream seller whose frozen desserts turn kids into killers, and Appofeniacs, a series of horror snippets exploring AI.

Sources indicate that other highlights include Nicolas Cage's Best Pancakes in the County, the Anthony Bourdain biopic Tony, and the Patricia Highsmith-inspired psychological thriller A Talent for Murder. There’s also The Beast, a new Samuel L. Jackson film where he stars as a President trying to survive a terrorist attack with only a wounded Secret Service Agent for protection. Happy watching.

Sources indicate that perhaps the biggest film of the year is finally available on streaming. Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey adapts the story of Odysseus (Matt Damon) to the screen in appropriately epic fashion and format, having him face giants, witches, sea monsters, mermaids, and much more as he tries to return home to his wife (Anne Hathaway) and son (Tom Holland).

Sources indicate that the Odyssey opens with a gentle warning: "A time of apparent magic," a gentle prod at audiences to both accept and question what they're about to see. Yet Ithaca, and the Palace of Odysseus, is all too devoid of magic. His wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) has spent the last 20 years waiting for her husband (Matt Damon) to return home from the Trojan War, while a small army of suitors vies to replace him. Running out of time before lead suitor Antinous (Robert Pattinson) can seal the deal, Odysseus' son Telemachus (Tom Holland) sets out on a journey to either find his dad or prove he's dead and claim the crown (either option seems fine for the young lad).

Netflix’s latest animated film takes the well-trodden story of Cinderella and reinvents it through a fresh perspective. It tells the story from the side of her evil stepsisters. The story follows Lilith (Ali Wong), who accidentally turns her sister Margot (Stephanie Tsu) into a frog. To bring her sister back, she has to team up with her estranged stepsister Cinderella (Amanda Seyfried) to save the kingdom.

Sources indicate that the star-studded cast of Steps works hard to give depth to characters who, for all intents and purposes, were completely shallow in their original tales. Wong is known for her sharpness and her comedy. She meshes well with this more modern take on the ugly stepsister, but she’s just as capable of hitting you where it hurts when the story calls for it. Her anger at being unaccepted and belittled by the people around her, while Cinderella only has to exist to be loved, is heartbreaking to watch.

It has been revealed that insidious: Out of the Further is finally out on Netflix. The film expands on the successful Blumhouse franchise, focusing on a different family. It follows Gemma (Amelia Eve), a single mother traumatized by a childhood dominated by an absent mother and a terrifying incident. As she begins to have strange dreams, she starts to scare her daughter and mirror her mother’s erratic behavior.

In a recent development, written and directed by Mary Kreutzer, Gentle Monster follows a concert pianist (Lea Seydoux) who relocates to the countryside after her husband claims burnout. As the film progresses, we learn that her husband is facing some serious accusations from the police.

According to recent reports, based on a pivotal summer in Anthony Bourdain’s life, Tony is set in 1975, following a 19-year-old fictional version of Bourdain who relocates to Provincetown to follow his high school crush. After a series of slips and disasters, he ends up getting a job as a dishwasher in a restaurant.

According to recent reports, nicolas Cage stars in this thriller, which has drawn comparisons to Tarantino, playing a criminal on the run from a botched heist. He hides in a diner, triggering a face-off with all sorts of enemies, including federal agents, criminals, and more, putting a seemingly innocent waitress and line cook at risk.

Eli Roth’s latest film follows a strange and mysterious ice cream man (Ari Millen) who serves frozen desserts that turn kids into violent killers.

According to recent reports, set in 1995, A Talent for Murder follows an editor from Upcoming York (Alden Ehrenreich) who’s been sent to the Swiss Alps to convince Patricia Highsmith (Helen Mirren) to write a new Tom Ripley novel. There, she challenges him to help her craft the perfect murder.

Appofeniacs contains various stories, all centered on the impact of AI. It follows a troll wreaking chaos on people’s lives by creating AI deepfakes, including a smear campaign, putting a man's life and career at risk, and more.

The Beast is an action-thriller starring Samuel L. Jackson. The premise is wild: the US President (Jackson), a former U.S. veteran, gets stranded at an international summit, with his protective detail wiped out in an attack. He’s left alone with a wounded Secret Service agent (Joel Kinnaman) as the two try to survive.
