💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I've been a fan of “Percy Jackson” for as long as I can remember.
  • It has been revealed that season 3 adapts “The Titan's Curse,” the third book in Riordan’s beloved series.
  • I’ve watched the first four episodes of season 3, and there’s plenty to get excited about.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I've been a fan of “Percy Jackson” for as long as I can remember. I still remember picking up the books for the first time as a kid and getting completely swept up in Rick Riordan’s world of Greek mythology, monsters and teenage demigods. It’s a franchise I’ve had a soft spot for ever since, so seeing it find a upcoming audience through Disney’s adaptation has been a real treat. And now, somehow, we’re already heading into "Percy Jackson and the Olympians" season 3. I can’t quite believe how swiftly that’s come around, but I’m certainly not complaining.

It has been revealed that season 3 adapts “The Titan's Curse,” the third book in Riordan’s beloved series. This time, Percy (Walker Scobell) and Grover (Aryan Simhadri) find themselves on a dangerous mission to rescue Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries), who has gone missing following an encounter with a mysterious upcoming threat. With the fate of Olympus hanging in the balance, Percy must contend with powerful enemies and a prophecy that could change everything. It’s another massive adventure for the young demigods, but one that comes with considerably higher stakes.

I’ve watched the first four episodes of season 3, and there’s plenty to get excited about. While the show still has the humor, friendship and sense of adventure that made me fall in love with the books in the first place, this latest chapter feels noticeably more mature. It’s an encouraging step forward for the Disney+ series, and one that makes me even more invested in seeing where these characters go next. Here’s what I thought of the first four episodes.

In a recent development, I’m Alix, a lifelong horror nerd who loves watching, reviewing and writing about the latest movies and TV reveals. When I’m not working through my ever-growing horror watchlist, I’m covering the biggest releases across streaming and film, including "VisionQuest" on Disney+, "The Institute" season 2 on MGM+, and "Guarding Stars" on Netflix.

Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” wastes little time setting a darker, more action-packed tone. It opens with Thalia Grace (Tamara Smart) hunting for Luke (Charlie Bushnell) in a parking garage, where she finds herself battling a dangerous monster. Percy soon crashes into the fight. Thalia isn’t particularly thrilled about needing his help, which establishes some immediate friction between the two demigods. The opening also introduces the season’s central mission, with Annabeth explaining that she needs Thalia’s help to rescue two young demigods, siblings Nico (Levi Chrisopulos) and Bianca di Angelo (Olive Abercrombie).

Sources indicate that book readers will understand the significance of these characters straight away, while show-only viewers will get a better idea as the season unfolds. Thankfully, the first episode doesn't take long to get the main story moving, either, as Annabeth is abducted, triggering Percy’s fatal flaw: his unwavering loyalty. He’s determined to get her back, no matter how dangerous the quest becomes. That sense of danger carries through the first four episodes, and I think it’s one of the season’s biggest improvements.

With the group getting older and the looming threat of war becoming increasingly difficult to ignore, the show feels noticeably more mature in its storytelling. Percy and his friends are exposed to greater dangers, and there’s a stronger sense that their actions could have serious consequences. It’s also great to see the series developing Percy’s abilities, particularly his control over water. His powers have felt somewhat underexplored in previous seasons, so watching him become more confident and capable with them is a welcome change. He’s clearly getting stronger, and I hope the remaining episodes continue to build on that.

Of course, you can't talk about “Percy Jackson” without mentioning Percabeth, and I know plenty of fans are just as invested in Percy and Annabeth’s developing relationship as they are in the Greek mythology. Thankfully, season 3 gives us a little more to enjoy on that front. It’s still very much a slow burn, with neither quite ready to acknowledge that their feelings might be more than friendship, but there’s a growing awareness that something special is there. The dance scene in episode 1 is a particularly lovely example of this. I suspect season 3 will give Percabeth fans plenty to get excited about.

It has been revealed that based on the first four episodes, season 3 is probably the strongest “Percy Jackson” season yet. I particularly appreciate is how much more attention is given to the emotional baggage these teenagers carry as the children of some incredibly powerful figures, many of whom seem largely uninterested in their own kids’ lives. including Thalia’s complicated relationship with Zeus. We get more of an insight into how these circumstances fuel their trauma and motives.

It gives the series a little more emotional depth without losing sight of the fun. The visual effects are also stronger, with the action sequences feeling grander and more cinematic than before. There’s a real sense that the show is becoming more ambitious with each season, and these early episodes have me excited to see what’s next. If the remaining episodes maintain this momentum, “Percy Jackson” could reach a whole latest level, and I can only hope Disney+ has more seasons covering the rest of the books in store.

The first two episodes of "Percy Jackson" season 3 is streaming on Disney+, with the final six episodes releasing in pairs every Friday through December 11, 2026.

#16825. Industry News: Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (856 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • Recent findings suggest that I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • It has been revealed that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

Recent findings suggest that I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

It has been revealed that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

If you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an problem with the Duo itself.

I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

Industry observers note that I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for shows and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

According to recent reports, multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

It has been revealed that after a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

According to recent reports, I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

Sources indicate that I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

According to recent reports, I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

The iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique fresh iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

According to recent reports, what has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week was a Skydance buyout deadline for employees to decide whether to accept a buyout offer, including at CBS News.

The offer came following the closing of Skydance’s purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as the tech giant seeks $6 billion in savings. The merger puts CBS News and CNN under the same corporate umbrella.

In a recent development, at CBS News, the buyout was accepted by employees across the news division, with the London bureau among the most impacted, sources familiar with the prepares stated. Some staffers on 60 Minutes also took the buyout, although none were in key lead editorial roles, according to a source. Related Stories News Donald Trump Touts "Unbelievable" Bipartisan Support For Federal Film & TV Incentive, Notes Theaters May Be Added: "It's Going To Happen" News 'MobLand' Season 3 Starts Shooting As Season 2 Finale Drops On Paramount+.

According to recent reports, in the Washington bureau, Mary Hager, senior executive producer of Face the Nation, announced her departure earlier this month after 35 years at the network, although CBS News did not say whether her exit was tied to the buyout offer. Anne Hsu, who has been executive producer, is moving to the network’s Hong Kong bureau. Watch on Deadline.

All told, less than 10% of staffers offered buyouts accepted them, according to a source. In its report on the buyouts, Status newsletter reported that dozens took the offer, including producers and members of the operational staff in London. The UK’s labor laws also require robust offers compared to the U.S., while there also has been some anxiety over the future with two major news brands under the same ownership.

In a recent development, while CNN and CBS News remain as separate news entities, media companies looking to cut costs often look to foreign bureaus for savings. And this week, Skydance CEO David Ellison said that while he’s “incredibly happy” operating CNN and CBS News as they are, there “might be some news sharing” in the future.

CNN’s buyout deadline was earlier this month.

CBS News went through a round of cuts last October and another round in March. The latest round represented about 6% of the workforce, or around 60 to 70 employees out of about 1,100.

It has been revealed that for country chart-topper Megan Moroney and pop hitmaker Alex Warren, a song isn’t necessarily finished when it leaves the studio. Sometimes, it needs a test drive.

Sources indicate that for Warren, listening to music in the car holds sentimental meaning. On his newly introduced album, Wildchild, he pays tribute to his late father, who died of cancer when Warren was just nine years old. Some of his most powerful musical memories with his dad are inseparable from time spent in the car.

“My only memory of music growing up was getting in the car and listening to my dad’s CDs, and John Mayer was his guy,” Warren said. “When my dad passed away, I got in his car and [Mayer’s album] came on. When I wrote this song for my dad called ‘Wildchild,’ I put his voice on it, and I asked [Mayer] to do a guitar solo on it, so my dad and John have a song.”.

Recent findings suggest that the car is also where Warren discovered Moroney’s music. He recalls listening to her breakout hit “Tennessee Orange” in the car with his wife, who knew every word.

“She knows that song like the back of her hand, and it’s really cool because she applies it to her own life,” Warren said of Moroney’s autobiographical debut, which tells the story of a die-hard Georgia football fan falling for a Tennessee Volunteers fan.

“It encapsulates the kind of music my fans like,” stated Moroney, whose sharp-eyed songwriting turns specific details into universal feelings that resonate with the masses.

Industry observers note that “It’s creative, it’s honest, there’s the hook, and it’s storytelling. I feel like at the root of all of my songs, that’s what it is. And obviously I’m a Georgia Bulldog, so it’s just very me.”.

Sources indicate that moroney and Warren may come from different corners of the music world, but the two found plenty of common ground during a conversation outside Fox & Locke, a storied live-music venue tucked into the rolling countryside of Leiper’s Fork, Tennessee. The discussion was part of Rolling Stone’s Musicians on Musicians series. This time, Lexus sought to connect two artists from different backgrounds in an entirely upcoming way by trading the usual lounge-like venues that host Musicians on Musicians conversations for the lounge-inspired quiet cabin of an all-electric 2027 Lexus TZ, which will make its debut this winter. In a recent development, as the conversation continued, Moroney and Warren learned that their paths to stardom have more than a few parallels. Both got an early boost from TikTok before breaking through with massive singles from their debut albums — Moroney with her five-times-platinum “Tennessee Orange,” Warren with his record-breaking “Ordinary.” Both have crossed genre lines through collaborations, and both released hit albums this year: Moroney’s autobiographical Cloud 9 and Warren’s deeply personal Wildchild. They also share a belief in one essential part of the creative process: the all-crucial “car test.”.

For Warren, that test played a pivotal role in one of the biggest songs of his career. After receiving an early, stripped-down version of “Ordinary” — little more than his voice and a piano — he played it for his wife while they were driving. Her reaction told him everything he needed to know. “She was like, ‘I want more of it!’”.

According to recent reports, the experience changed the way he shares fresh music. “Now I only show people songs in my car.”.

In a recent development, he might be onto something. Whether you’re a professional musician or more of a carpool-karaoke type, there’s something about hearing a song on the road that changes the experience. A lyric lands a little harder. A melody feels a little bigger. And sometimes, the right song at the right moment can turn a daily drive into something worth remembering. Of course, when your life revolves around music, sometimes the best soundtrack is no soundtrack at all. Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1150 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • In a recent development, GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most notable tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

In a recent development, let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

In a recent development, game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

Sources indicate that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

Industry observers note that more importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

It has been revealed that I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

In a recent development, the DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

Recent findings suggest that the Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

Sources indicate that if you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for fresh hardware, this might be your best bet.

Industry observers note that xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

AirPods got a variety of new features this fall in iOS 27, several of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179). Here’s everything new.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods owners thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

Sources indicate that with Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

Recent findings suggest that airPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

Recent findings suggest that you can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

Apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym.

For most AirPods users, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

AirPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the newly introduced Siri. It will let people do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:.

According to recent reports, earlier this year when AirTag 2 launched, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of latest AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

Now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.

Looking for a genuinely cool tech gadget for less than $25? I’ve got just the one. The Casio WSB1000-1AV is a tough-built digital watch beaming with 1990s charm, but also a surprising smattering of modern tech niceties. Best of all, it’s 65% off for Black Friday.

Need an office Secret Santa/gift exchange option that won’t break the bank? Not sure what to get for your “cool” Gen Z cousin or technologically challenged parents? The answer is this deeply discounted $22 Casio watch, which, on pretty much any other day, would cost you $64. Here are five reasons why.

Marked down from $64 to just $22, this retro-1990s Casio digital watch features an onboard step counter and Bluetooth antenna for automatic time adjustments.

Hidden behind the screen of this seemingly ordinary digital watch is a Bluetooth antenna. Why would a dumb watch need Bluetooth? To pair it with your smartphone, of course. Once paired, the Casio WSB1000 automatically corrects the time based on your smartphone’s clock.

Industry observers note that this means there’s no need to fuss with resetting the time when traveling across time zones. The bare-bones smartphone app can also be used to set or cancel an alarm on the watch, a timer, a stopwatch, and other basic functions.

Lastly, the onboard Bluetooth plays a key role in this next feature.

You’ll notice that the Casio WSB1000 has the words “Step Tracker” printed above the LCD. This refers to this little watch’s automatic step-counting feature. Who needs the best Apple Watch or the latest Fitbit?

According to recent reports, like an actual smartwatch or fitness tracker, customers can set daily step-count targets. The WSB1000 not only tracks your total and displays it on the watch’s LCD, but it also shows a dynamic graphic of your progress toward that day’s goal.

Bluetooth, meanwhile, is used to ping that step-count data back to your smartphone.

According to recent reports, with onboard Bluetooth and automatic step-count tracking, battery life must be pretty short? Surprisingly, no. Casio says that the common drugstore CR2016 battery in the watch should keep it powered for approximately two years.

Afterwards, a battery swap should be a relatively painless, affordable process, done either at home (if you're savvy) or at your local jewelry store.

While the Casio WSB1000 isn’t quite as durable as watches in the brand’s legendary G-Shock range, this digital wonder is rated for 100 meters of water resistance, the same as the latest Apple Watch Ultra 4. It also boasts a shock-resistant (though not shockproof), lightweight resin case.

In a recent development, ultimately, for less than $25, you're not just getting a Bluetooth-capable digital watch with step counting; you're getting the Casio WSB1000, a 90s timepiece with a design that's Tom Cruise-running-atop-a-moving-train-cool; it's Keanu Reeves-stopping-a-speeding-bus-badass... etc.

And even if your intended recipient overlooks the step tracking and tosses this watch in a drawer for occasional use, when they do eventually pull it out and pop it on, you can be sure the time and date will be spot-on thanks to the Bluetooth connection.

The album’s August release date marked two milestones: the first time a member had released solo music and the first release since Adam Yauch (aka MCA) died in 2012 of cancer. Speaking to Rolling Stone earlier this year, Mike D reflected on what it took to make an album for the first time without Yauch and Adam Horovitz (aka Ad-Rock) by his side.

According to recent reports, “With Yauch, there was so much intertwined about him being an older-brother figure to me, to what he represented to us being in this band together,” he explained. “I had to go through all that … I grieve him because I don’t get to live my life being able to call him up and say, “Yauch, you wouldn’t believe this thing happened, but I have to tell you about this … But I can think about what he might be thinking, or what his relationship would be to this thing that I’m going through, or just me making this record and what he might say.”.

When iOS 27.3 launches next month, it will include a variety of upgrades for Apple TV, Apple Music, Siri AI, iCloud+, the iPhone Duo, and more.

Another tentpole addition is an all-new Apple Health app, which was first unveiled back in September when new Apple Watch models debuted.

Taylor Swift certainly brought her fans with her back to Country Music’s Biggest Night.

The 60th annual ceremony hit a seven-year audience high with 7.62 million total live + same-day viewers tuning in for the CMA Awards on Wednesday, per Nielsen Big Data + Panel.

The star-studded show, which featured Swift’s return to the CMA stage after 13 years to perform a mash up of Toy Story 5‘s “I Knew It, I Knew You” and her classic “Our Song,” also managed a 1.01 rating among adults 18-49 — a three-year best.

It has been revealed that hosted by Lainey Wilson for the third year in a row, the telecast was up 26% versus last year’s audience of 6.03 million, and ranked as the No. 1 program across broadcast and cable on Wednesday night.

Disney kicked things off the night before with Darius, Dolly and 60 Years of Celebration: Countdown to the CMAs with Robin Roberts. The special took viewers backstage ahead of the award show and earned 2.99 million views. The annual ABC News primetime special got its best viewership in three years. Watch on Deadline.

The 60th Annual CMA Awards is a production of the Country Music Association. Robert Deaton serves as executive producer, Alan Carter is director, and Jon Macks is head writer.

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink rapidly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

In a recent development, these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 rolled out at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also vital to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Tech Report: Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a new filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the company complies.
  • As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct owners to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.
  • Apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a new filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the company complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct owners to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a upcoming filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its new filing, Epic says Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the firm of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

Industry observers note that apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple notes decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s new CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”.

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

According to recent reports, under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

It has been revealed that given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”.

According to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a fresh order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

E.J. Carroll, a veteran character actor whose credits include The Deuce, Boardwalk Empire, Blue Bloods three Law & Order series and Grand Theft Auto V, died November 19. He was 66. His rep Jon Mason of Mason-Lewis Entertainment stated Carroll died suddenly while en route to a voice-over booking, but he did not provide a cause of death.

Recent findings suggest that born on May 21, 1960, Carroll appeared in features, television, short films and video games during a nearly three-decade screen career. His first screen credit was playing a cop in a 1998 episode of NBC’s Law & Order, and he would appear as other characters in three other episodes through 2004. He also had roles in two early-2000s episodes of its juggernaut spinoff Law & Order: SVU and two more in Law & Order: Criminal Intent that decade.

He would appear in a number of movies during the later 2000s and into the 2010s including Darren Aronfsky’s acclaimed 2009 drama The Wrestler, along with The Cake Eaters, The Capers, The Winning Season, The Hungry Ghosts, A Fish Story and the Robert De Niro-Kate Beckinsale pic Everything’s Fine, among others.

Carroll played Sheriff Victor Sickles in two 2012 episodes of HBO’s lauded period crime drama Boardwalk Empire, from Tenrence Winter and MArtin Scorsese and starring Steve Buscemi, appeared in episode of FX’s Glenn Close-Rose Byrne legal thriller Damages that same year. He went on to guest on NBC’s The Blacklist, CBS’ Blue Bloods, HBO’s High Maintenance, FX’s Pose and Netflix’s Marvel series The Punisher.

In a recent development, he landed perhaps his most recognizable role in 2017, recurring on the HBO’ ‘s The Deuce as Fat Mooney, who ran a Latest York City sex shop owned by Frankie Martino (James Franco). He appeared in a half-dozen episodes of the series about the rise of the porn industry in the 1970s and ’80s.

Recent findings suggest that most recently, Carroll filmed a role in A Delicate Arrangement, the upcoming film written and produced by Jayce Bartok and directed by Nick Sandow. It stars Carla Gugino as Vivien Leigh in the true story of two-time Oscar winning actress’ relationship with a Philadelphia florist (Matthew Modine). David Hyde Pierce also stars in the film, which is in post-production.

“E.J. Carroll was a consummate actor known and loved for his intense commitment to the characters he played,” said who noted that Carroll was passionate about A Delicate Arrangement and helped ensure the project would be completed. “There isn’t an actor in Newly introduced York that hadn’t worked with or crossed paths with E.J., known for stealing scenes alongside Robert De Niro, Mickey Rourke, Bruce Dern and most recently Jalen Brunson and Quinta Brunson. He will be greatly missed by the acting community which he lived for.”.

RELATED: Celebrities Who’ve Voiced Characters In ‘Grand Theft Auto’.

Carroll also voiced a character in the blockbuster 2013 video game Grand Theft Auto and played Dr. Scott in The Rocky Horror Tribute Show, a concert version of The Rocky Horror Show that played one night only in 2007 as a benefit for cancer charities Acting for a Cure/Komen for the Cure.

Information about survivors or a memorial service was not immediately available.
